title: Customer replay guidance + incident evidence roadmap (partial routing fallback, 2030-06-28)
content:
Summary:
On 2030-06-28 between 02:12 and 03:45 UTC we experienced a partial routing fallback that routed a subset of customer inference requests to a lower-capacity model variant. This produced higher-latency responses and, in some cases, subtle differences in embeddings and structured outputs for affected tenants. This doc is intended as a customer-facing status update + practical replay/evidence roadmap to help customers validate impact, reconcile results, and decide on remediation paths.

High-level impact:
- Affected window: ~02:12–03:45 UTC (intermittent, multiple waves).
- Scope: ~3.8% of total inference traffic across two EU regions, primarily tenants on shared-hosting with dynamic routing enabled.
- Symptoms observed by tenants: increased tail latency (95th p50->p95 jump), truncated streaming chunks for a small percentage of sessions, embedding inconsistency for batch reranks processed during the window.
- Customer-facing consequence: non-deterministic quality regressions (rare), delayed responses, and the need for re-ranking/replay for a subset of requests. No data exfiltration or unauthorized access detected.

Immediate mitigations we enacted (during incident):
- 02:20 UTC: We detected abnormal routing metrics and automatically triggered safe-mode to stop dynamic fallback policies.
- 02:33 UTC: Scoped routing override applied to pin traffic to the pre-fallback model variants for critical tenants.
- 02:55 UTC: Global rollback of the new routing policy; routing controllers reverted to stable baseline.
- 03:12 UTC: Cache warmers and KV-preserve process restarted to reduce transient prefix misses.

Root cause (current engineering summary):
- A change in the routing policy evaluation engine interacted with a recently-deployed kernel heuristic in the serving runtime. Under a narrow set of session length and token distribution patterns the routing evaluator misclassified compatible model variants, allowing the fallback path to be selected for some requests.
- The fallback model variant is functionally compatible but has a different quantization/embedding projection, which explains the small embedding vector shifts and structural output truncations in streaming mode.

Why this feels different from a pure capacity outage:
- Not an availability loss: service remained online and returned responses.
- Quality drift: the failure mode is correctness/consistency drift rather than pure downtime, which can be harder for customers to detect without targeted checks.

Customer guidance: validating and reconciling affected requests
We want customers to be able to: (A) identify which requests were impacted, (B) replay them deterministically against the stable model, and (C) verify whether replays restore expected behavior. Below is a practical checklist and commands your engineering teams can use.

1) Identify candidate impacted time ranges and tenant buckets
- Start with: 2030-06-28 02:12 UTC -> 2030-06-28 03:45 UTC.
- Focus on: tenants using shared-hosting and dynamic routing. If you are on Dedicated or Private with pinned models, you were likely unaffected.
- Use your logs to search for: model_variant changes, routing_reason=="fallback", or sudden p95 latency spikes. Example query (pseudo):
  - logs.query("service:inference AND timestamp:[2030-06-28T02:00 TO 2030-06-28T04:00] AND routing_reason:fallback")

2) Export candidate request traces and compressed evidence bundle
- Collect request ids, timestamps, model_variant id, tokens_in, tokens_out, and kv-cache markers.
- Example evidence bundle fields we recommend saving: request_id, tenant_id, timestamp_utc, original_model_variant, served_model_variant, request_payload_snippet, response_snippet, embedding_vector_base64.

3) Replay recommendations (server-side deterministic replay)
- Replay against the pre-fallback model variant id: model-redwood-v2-stable-2029-11 (example).
- Use streaming flag disabled for deterministic full response comparisons.
- Sample replay command (pseudo-API):
  - POST /v1/replay
    headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
    body: {"request_id": "<id>", "target_model": "model-redwood-v2-stable-2029-11", "preserve_kv_cache": true} 
- If you need us to run replays on your behalf, see the Contact section below; include the request id list and a short priority list.

4) Automating verification: suggested diffs
- Embeddings: compute cosine similarity between original_vector and replay_vector; we expect > 0.995 for functionally equivalent responses in most workloads.
- Structured outputs: validate canonical JSON schema equality or semantic equivalence checks (e.g., idempotent canonicalization + hash).
- Streaming/truncations: compare length and last-chunk checksum.

Evidence package we will provide to affected customers
We will assemble and share, per-tenant, a signed evidence bundle containing:
- Operator timeline snapshot and routing controller logs for the impacted window.
- List of request_ids we identified as routed to fallback variants (CSV).
- A short explanation of the model_variant differences (quantization and projection notes).
- If requested: replay outputs from our controlled replays and checksum diffs.

Compensation and remediation offer
- If you confirm measurable customer-facing regressions (quality or revenue impact) from our replay verification, we will:
  - Offer a one-time service credit proportional to affected request volume (subject to review).
  - Prioritize a dedicated engineering audit and create a customer-specific mitigation plan (timeline and checkpoints).

Engineering action plan and timeline (what we will do next)
- 2030-06-29: Complete post-incident RCA doc (internal) with deep kernel+routing interaction traces and open PR for potential fixes.
- 2030-07-02: Roll out a conservative routing policy gate that requires explicit compatibility checks for embedding projection signatures.
- 2030-07-05: Add a customer-visible flag to disable dynamic routing per-route for tenants that prefer pinned behavior without a full migration.
- Ongoing: Add a regression alert that monitors embedding drift (cosine similarity histogram) per-tenant and triggers early rollback.

How we classify severity and what this means for SLAs
- We consider this a service-quality incident (SQi) rather than a full outage. For tenants under SLA who experienced measurable degradation of correctness, we will open a severity review to determine whether SLA credits apply under the customer agreement.

If you want Redwood to run replays for you (short guide)
- Provide: tenant_id, list of request_ids (max 5k per job), and priority. We will queue and run controlled replays within 72 hours and return a signed evidence bundle. For large-volume needs, we will coordinate a schedule and an engineering lead.

Contact and escalation
- Primary CS contact: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai) — for replay requests and compensation intake.
- Engineering lead: Ethan Rodriguez (ethan@redwood.ai) — for technical validation and traces.
- If you need immediate assistance or a scheduled replay, include "REPLAY:PRIORITY" in the subject line.

Appendix A — Minimal verification checklist for customers (copyable)
- [ ] Pull request ids from your ingestion logs for 2030-06-28 02:12-03:45 UTC.
- [ ] Confirm model_variant differences in returned metadata.
- [ ] Request Redwood replay for a prioritized sample.
- [ ] Compute cosine similarity on embedding vectors, compare structured outputs.

Appendix B — Short technical notes for platform engineers
- Routing evaluator change: defective heuristic evaluated compatibility on a hashed token-window signature that did not include projection metadata.
- Serving runtime interaction: a kernel heuristic that chooses a quantized matrix path triggered for certain short sequences, inadvertently exposing minor numeric shifts in embedding outputs.
- Long-term controls: require projection-signature binding in the routing contract and add canary-scale tests for embedding histograms across releases.

Closing note:
We regret the customer impact and take any drift in correctness seriously. Our goal with this doc is to make validation, replay, and reconciliation as straightforward as possible for engineering teams so you can decide whether to accept replays, request remediation, or apply local compensations. We will follow up with per-tenant evidence bundles and a final customer-facing postmortem once the internal RCA is complete.

-- Maya Thompson, Customer Success (on behalf of incident ops and serving runtime)
